items.snippet: 지난달 21일 서부전선 비무장지대(DMZ) 지뢰 폭발사건이 발생한 지 한 달째에 접어들고 있지만 정부는 북한에 대해 구체적인 “상응조치”를 내놓지 않고 있다. 김정은 북한 국무위원장의 여동생인 김여정 노동당 총무부장이 지뢰 폭발이 자작극이라며 “즉시적이고 가차없는 보복”을 가하겠다고 위협했지만 정부는 2015년 목함지뢰 사건 당시 2주 만에 보냈던 유엔 안전보장이사회 서한조차 대응 여부를 결정하지 못하고 있는 것. 외교부는 20일 “국제사회를 대상으로 폭발의 원인이 인위적으로 매설된 북한군 지뢰로 최종 판명되었고 이는 명백한 정전협정 위반인 점을 설명하고 있다”면서도 “유엔 관련 (조치 등) 추가 조치에 대해 관계부처와 대응방안을 계속 검토할 것으로 생각한다”고 밝혔다. 앞서 우리 군은 북한 지뢰로 최종 판명되면 상응하는 조치를 하겠다고 밝혔...

items.title: 메가특구 주52시간 “예외” “불가” 법안 동시에 낸 與
items.snippet: 여당이 전남광주 반도체 클러스터 등 메가특구를 지원하기 위한 ‘초광역특구법(메가특구법)’을 발의하면서 고소득·연구직 노동자의 주 52시간제 예외 등 노동특례를 포함시킨 안과 제외한 안을 동시에 발의하기로 했다. 노동특례를 놓고 갈등이 지속되자 “연내 통과”를 못 박으며 속도를 강조했던 여당이 결론을 미룬 것이다. 더불어민주당 한병도 원내대표는 20일 “주요 쟁점인 노동시간 특례 등을 둘러싸고 다양한 의견이 있음을 잘 알고 있다”며 “특례를 포함한 안과 포함하지 않은 안 두 가지 법안을 제출한다”고 밝혔다. 민주당은 두 법안을 향후 병합 심사해 최종안을 마련하고, 여러 부처와 상임위에 걸친 쟁점을 다루기 위해 여야가 참여하는 국회 특별위원회 설치도 검토하기로 했다. 한 원내대표는 “처리 시점을 못 박지 않고 충분한 숙의와 토론을 거치겠다”고 했...

items.title: 임명장 다음날 국무회의 참석한 중수청장… 野 “정치 수사화될 판”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 20일 국무회의에 참석한 김지용 중대범죄수사청장에게 “화이트칼라 범죄나 권력형 부패 범죄, 증권·금융범죄 등 중대 범죄에 대해서 네 편 내 편 가르지 말고 일체의 성역 없이 엄단함으로써 중대범죄수사청장의 존재 의의와 필요성을 증명해 주시기 바란다”고 말했다. 김 청장은 이날 취임 후 처음으로 국무회의에 참석했다. 국민의힘은 독립성이 보장돼야 할 수사기관장의 국무회의 참석이 부적절하다고 지적하면서 “수사의 정치화는커녕 정치가 수사화될 판”이라고 비판했다. ● 李, 국무회의 나온 중수청장에 “성역 없는 수사” 이 대통령은 이날 오전 청와대에서 열린 국무회의에서 김 청장을 향해 “수사와 기소를 완전히 분리하고 공소청과 중수청의 소속 부처까지 달리하는 검찰개혁이 제도적으로 완비됐다”며 “중수청이 독립적인 중대 범죄 수사기관으로 새출발...

items.title: 정부, 우크라 대사 소환 이어 공관원 절반 철수
items.snippet: 정부가 20일 우크라이나에 주재하는 한국대사관 공관원 절반가량을 철수시키기로 했다. 정부가 8일 박기창 주우크라이나 대사를 소환했는데도 우크라이나가 북한군 포로의 한국 송환 비공개 합의를 깬 것을 공개 사과하지 않자 추가 조치를 취한 것이다. 박두순 외교부 대변인은 20일 정례브리핑에서 “주우크라이나 대사 소환 조치 이후에도 우크라이나 측의 전향적 조치가 없는 상황”이라며 “우크라이나 전역에 걸친 공습 위협이 상존해 안전 확보가 어려운 점 등을 고려해 공관원 일부 철수를 결정했다”고 밝혔다. 해외 공관원 철수는 2015년 주리비아 대사관과 2021년 주아프가니스탄 대사관 사례 이후 처음이다. 다만 윤지완 대사대리와 공관원 절반가량은 현지에 남아 최소한의 외교 활동과 수십 명의 현지 교민 대피 지원 등 영사 활동을 이어갈 방침이다. 정부는 박...

items.title: 李, ‘3기 신도시’ 인천 계양지구 찾아 “신속 공급이 부동산 정책 성패 갈라”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령은 20일 3기 신도시 중 처음으로 올해 12월부터 입주가 시작되는 인천 계양지구를 찾아 현장을 점검하고 “3기 신도시에서의 신속한 주택 공급은 부동산 정책의 성패를 가르는 중요한 분기점이 될 것”이라며 주택 공급을 강조했다. 이 대통령은 이날 주택공급 현장 간담회를 갖고 “비상사태다”라며 “예측 가능한 공급을 통해 시장의 불안감을 해소하고 궁극적으로는 국민의 주거 안정을 이루는 데 있어서 3기 신도시가 핵심적인 역할을 해 내야겠다”며 이같이 말했다. 이어 “이미 발표한 공급 정책이 제대로 이행되지 못하는 것 같은 모습을 보이면 부동산 정책 전반에 대한 국민의 신뢰도가 떨어질 수밖에 없다”고 했다. 한국갤럽 여론조사에서 7월 4주 차부터 부동산 정책이 대통령 직무수행 부정평가 이유 1위를 기록하는 상황에서 재차 속도전을 강조한 것...

items.title: 김정은 뇌출혈설 확산… 北, 사진 공개
items.snippet: 북한 관영매체 노동신문은 김정은 북한 국무위원장(오른쪽)이 19일 딸 주애와 함께 ‘새 제품 개발과 질 제고 열풍’을 주제로 열린 ‘전국 피복, 신발 전시회’에 참석했다고 20일 보도했다. 이날 해외 온라인 커뮤니티 등에서 김 위원장이 뇌출혈로 중국 베이징의 병원으로 긴급 이송됐다는 확인되지 않은 내용이 확산한 가운데 북한 매체가 김 위원장의 행보를 공개한 것이다.

items.title: “정전협정 위반”에도 상응조치 없는새, 北 “힘에는 힘” 위협 높여
items.snippet: 정부가 서부전선 비무장지대(DMZ) 북한 지뢰 폭발사건이 ‘명백한 정전협정 위반’이라는 결론을 내리고도 뚜렷한 ‘상응조치’를 내놓지 못하고 있는 가운데 북한은 잇따라 위협 수위를 높이고 있다. 19일 접경지역 전력 증강과 대남 확성기 방송 재개까지 거론한 데 이어 20일에는 한미·미일 연합군사훈련에 “강력한 힘의 선택이 적용될 것”이라고 위협했다. 정부는 ‘단호한 대응’을 강조하고 있지만 상응 조치를 두고는 정부 내 이견으로 별다른 진척을 보이지 못하고 있다.● 軍 감시장비 추가 설치… 북한은 잇단 위협 담화 국방부는 20일 김여정 북한 노동당 총무부장이 대남확성기 방송 재개 등 적반하장식 위협을 쏟아낸 데 대해 “(북한이) 추가 도발을 감행할 경우 단호히 응징할 것”이라고 밝혔다. “북한이 (대남 확성기 방송을 재개)한다고 하면 비례적 대응...

items.title: 정부 DMZ 조사, 유엔사 거부로 2년넘게 중단
items.snippet: 정부가 2020년부터 진행해온 비무장지대(DMZ) 내부 조사가 유엔군사령부의 출입 승인 거부로 2년 5개월째 중단된 상태인 것으로 나타났다. 유엔사는 올 3월 DMZ 범위를 정하는 남방한계선(SLL)을 새로 설정했다며 통일부의 남북출입사무소 역사관 관할권에 이의를 제기해 한때 역사관 운영이 중단됐던 것으로 드러났다. 20일 통일부 등에 따르면 DMZ 내부를 조사하는 정부 조사원에 대한 유엔사의 출입 승인이 2024년 5월부터 이뤄지지 않고 있다. DMZ 내부 조사는 2018년 남북정상회담에서 합의한 ‘DMZ 평화지대화’ 후속 조치다. 2020년부터 생태계(기후에너지환경부) 산림자원(산림청) 유네스코 세계유산 잠정목록(국가유산청), 2022년부터 DMZ 내부에 있던 마을(통일부)에 대한 조사가 이뤄져 왔다. 하지만 유엔사는 윤석열 정부 시절인...

items.title: 李 “북핵은 최후 방어용” 언급 논란… “北에 잘못된 시그널 줄수도”
items.snippet: 이재명 대통령이 북한 핵무기가 “최후 방어 무기에 해당한다”고 언급한 것을 두고 야권에서 “북한을 옹호한다”는 공세에 나서면서 논란이 커지고 있다. 북한이 전술핵을 포함한 핵탄두 및 투발 수단 다종화를 통해 핵 역량을 고도화하는 가운데 북핵 위험성을 ‘체제 방어용’으로 평가절하했다는 것. 전시작전통제권 전환 당위성을 설명하며 북핵이 전작권 전환 변수가 되기 어렵다는 취지이지만 자칫 북한에 잘못된 시그널을 줄 수 있다는 지적도 나온다.● 野 “北 조선노동당 대변인” 반발 이 대통령의 이 발언은 19일 기자간담회에서 전작권 관련 질의를 받고 “우리 스스로 방위를 감당할 수 있다”는 설명을 하는 과정에서 나왔다. 이 대통령은 핵 전력을 뺀 재래식 군사력이 세계 5위이고, 국방비 지출 수준이 북한의 연간 총생산(GDP) 다 합친 것의 1.5배가량 된...

items.title: 해군 “2040년대 초까지 3만t급 ‘드론 항모’ 확보”
items.snippet: 해군이 2040년 초까지 3만 t급 이상의 ‘유·무인전력모함’을 확보할 계획이라고 20일 밝혔다. 문재인 정부 때부터 경항공모함 도입을 적극 추진했지만, 현대전에서 드론 등 무인전력의 위력이 입증되면서 유·무인전력모함으로 전력 증강 계획을 변경한 것. 해군은 이날 국회 국방위원회 국정감사 업무보고 자료에서 지난해 10월 경항모 건조 사업을 유·무인전력모함으로 소요를 수정 제기했고, 합동참모본부가 현재 검토 중이라고 설명했다. 연내 소요 수정을 최종 결정한 뒤 2040년대 초까지 전력화를 목표로 하고 있다는 것이다. ‘드론항모’로도 불리는 유·무인전력모함에는 해상무인전투기와 감시정찰 및 자폭용 드론 등 무인전력 위주로 탑재된다. 해군이 추진하는 유·무인전력모함은 길이 270m, 폭 70m, 배수량은 3만 t급 이상으로 기존에 도입을 검토한 경항...

items.title: 與 ‘메가특구 주52시간 예외’ 눈치보며 시간끌기… 연내 도입 불투명

items.title: ‘소방 빨대-쭉쭉’ 논란에, 與 내부 “이대론 수도권 총선 망해”

items.title: “현장 구매 되나요?”… ‘오프라인’ 말고 ‘in person’

items.title: “국가직 된 지 6년, 바뀐 건 명찰뿐”
items.snippet: 2020년 4월 1일, 소방공무원 신분이 지방직에서 국가직으로 바뀌었다. 지역마다 다른 소방 인력과 장비 격차를 줄이고 소방에 대한 국가 책임을 강화하겠다는 차원에서 정부와 여야가 합의한 결과였다. 국가직으로 전환된 지 6년이 흐른 지금, 추미애 경기지사의 ‘소방은 재정 빨대’ 발언을 계기로 소방관이 국가직에 걸맞은 처우와 지원을 받고 있는지를 두고 논란이 일고 있다.

items.title: 같은 국가직인데… 경찰청은 국가 예산, 소방청은 지자체 예산
items.snippet: 소방관은 국가직 공무원이지만 월급과 장비 구입비는 대부분 지방자치단체가 부담한다. 올해 전국 소방 예산 8조5949억원 중 지자체 몫은 7조6151억원(88.6%)이다. 국가가 지원하는 예산은 10% 정도다. 내년에는 지원금이 약 2900억원(27.6%) 줄어든다. 2020년 지역 간 소방 인력의 격차를 줄이겠다며 소방공무원을 지방직에서 국가직으로 전환했지만 예산 구조는 그대로인 것이다. 지자체에서는 “국가직으로 바뀐 지 6년이 지났는데 부담은 여태껏 지자체가 지고 있다”는 불만이 나온다. 전문가들은 “국가와 지자체의 소방 예산 분담 구조를 다시 짜야 한다”고 지적한다.

items.title: 도쿄보다 많은 서울 공중화장실… 정작 외국인은 “못 찾겠어요”
items.snippet: 인도네시아에서 온 관광객 애슐리(19)양은 지난 18일 서울 마포구 망원시장을 구경하다가 화장실을 찾느라 애를 먹었다. 구글맵에 ‘restroom(화장실)’을 검색했지만 반경 50m 안에는 한 곳도 표시되지 않았다. 화장실을 찾아 15분을 헤맸다는 애슐리양은 “구글맵에 나온 공중화장실도 건물 안에 있어 입구를 찾기 어려웠다”고 했다.

items.title: 송파 경찰병원 의사 부족한데, 1253억 들여 아산에 또 추진
items.snippet: 서울 송파구에 있는 경찰병원은 경찰 공무원 진료를 전담하는 경찰청장 소속 국립병원이다. 그런데 경찰병원이 전문의·전공의 등 의료진을 제대로 채우지 못해 진료 시간까지 줄이고 있다. 이런 상황에서 경찰은 의사 58명이 필요한 제2경찰병원 건립을 추진하고 있다. 경찰청이 국민의힘 서명옥 의원실에 제출한 자료를 보면, 지난 8월 기준 경찰병원 정원 678명 가운데 52명이 공석이었다. 의사는 22명이 정원에 모자랐다. 전문의가 정원 75명 중 9명, 전공의는 정원 48명 중 13명이 공석이었다. 2021년부터 올해까지 의원면직으로 경찰병원을 떠난 전문의는 28명. 이에 따라 경찰병원 진료 시간도 총 23세션, 69시간이 줄었다. 진료 환자 수도 2023년 32만8090명에서 2025년 27만5434명으로 줄었다.

items.title: 광수단, 유력인사 수사 지지부진… 김승원·한동훈 의혹까지 맡을 듯
items.snippet: 서울경찰청은 19일 김승원(더불어민주당) 의원과 한동훈(무소속) 의원 관련 의혹 사건을 서울청 광역수사단에 배당할 예정이라고 밝혔다. 유시민씨 관련 명예훼손 고발 사건도 광수단이 맡았다. 검찰 폐지 후 경찰이 굵직한 사건을 떠맡으면서 서울청 광수단이 바빠지고 있다. 서울청 광수단이 맡을 김승원 의원 사건은 김 의원이 코로나 치료제 개발 업체 제넨셀 청탁을 받고 식품의약품안전처에 임상 시험 관련 민원을 전달했다는 의혹이다. 한동훈 의원 사건은 김승원 의원이 법무부 장관 후보자에 지명되자 한 의원이 제넨셀 청탁 관련 의혹을 제기하면서 검찰 내부 수사 자료를 공개했다는 의혹 사건이다.

items.title: 전자발찌 채우면 뭐하나… 범죄자 870명 늘때 관리자는 20명 줄어
items.snippet: 지난 13일 인천 남동구 구월동에서 흉기 난동을 벌인 최충락(59)은 전자발찌를 차고 있었다. 전자발찌는 재범 위험이 큰 범죄자 위치를 실시간으로 파악하는 장치다. 재범을 막기 위해서다. 하지만 전자발찌는 살인 미수 전과가 있는 최충락의 범행을 막지 못했다. 19일 경기 성남에서는 경찰에 신변 보호를 요청해 스마트워치를 지급받은 60대 여성이 전 남편이 휘두른 흉기에 찔려 다치는 사건이 발생했다. 스마트워치는 성폭력·가정폭력 피해자 등 신변 보호가 필요한 사람에게 지급된다. 버튼을 누르면 곧바로 경찰에 도움을 요청할 수 있는 기기다. 이처럼 범죄 가해자를 관리하고 피해자를 보호하기 위한 장치를 도입했지만 강력 범죄를 막지 못하는 일이 잇따르고 있다.

items.title: 가평엔 벌써 노란 카펫 깔렸네
items.snippet: 19일 오후 경기 가평군 북면의 한 카페 뒤뜰. 전날 내린 가을비에 은행잎이 우수수 떨어졌다. 어느새 노란 카펫이 깔렸다. 비가 그친 뒤 공기도 한결 선선해졌다. 한 시민이 가을 풍경을 감상하고 있다. 기상청은 21일 또 비가 내린 뒤 기온이 더 떨어질 것이라고 예상했다.

items.title: “한복 바르게 입으면 더 아름다워요”
items.snippet: 19일 서울 경복궁 경회루 앞에서 진행된 ‘한복 바르게 입기 캠페인’ 발대식 참여자들이 한복 차림으로 기념사진을 찍고 있다. 이번 캠페인은 문화체육관광부, 국가유산청, 한국공예·디자인문화진흥원이 마련한 것으로, 연말까지 경복궁 인근 한복 대여점에서 할인 행사 등이 진행된다.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [디자인·건축 이야기] 우주선 닮은 미술관, 호수에 비치는 호텔… 곡선미 주목받는 세계적 건축가예요
items.snippet: 최근 건축계에서 가장 화제인 작품 중 하나가 지난달 개관한 미국 로스앤젤레스의 ‘루카스 내러티브 아트 뮤지엄’입니다. ‘스타워즈’로 유명한 영화감독 조지 루카스와 그의 아내 멜로디 홉슨이 사재 10억달러(약 1조3400억원)를 털어 만들었어요. 독특한 외관이 특징인데요. 곡선으로 휘어지고 솟은 건물은 지상에 착륙한 우주선처럼 보여요. 거대한 건물 한가운데를 아치처럼 들어 올려 그 아래에 광장을 만들었어요. 광장 위로는 4개 층을 관통하는 타원형 천창을 통해 하늘을 올려다볼 수 있죠.

items.title: [신문은 선생님] [사소한 역사] 한 번 걸리면 50일까지 앓았던 ‘고뿔’ 세종대왕이 감기 꾀병 부린 까닭은?
items.snippet: 올해는 독감 유행이 일찍 시작됐어요. 질병관리청은 지난달 11일 전국에 독감 유행 주의보를 발령했습니다. 현대에는 독감이나 감기에 걸리면 해열제를 비롯해 다양한 약을 써요. 하지만 이런 약이 없던 과거에는 감기에 걸리는 걸 더욱 걱정했습니다. 과거 우리나라에서 감기를 부르는 말은 고뿔이었어요. ‘코에 불이 난다’는 의미인데요. 감기에 걸려 기침을 하고 콧물을 쏟아내면 코가 아프기 때문에 그런 명칭이 붙은 것으로 보입니다. 현대에는 일반 감기와 인플루엔자 바이러스가 일으키는 독감을 서로 구분하지만, 둘을 명확히 나눌 수 없었던 과거에는 감기 자체에 걸리는 것을 경계했죠.

items.title: Two-qubit cryo-CMOS control of a spin register in diamond
items.abstract: Utility-scale quantum technologies will not only require a well-performing quantum platform, but also classical control hardware that is scalable, efficient, and meets the design requirements set by the quantum system of interest. One approach is the application of silicon CMOS technology, a highly scalable and mature technology, to design application-specific integrated circuits (ASIC) that are optimized for the quantum system. In this work, we present two-qubit control of electron and nuclear spins in NV centres in diamond, using a cryogenic CMOS qubit controller integrated with a diamond quantum device in a cryostat. Using Gate Set Tomography (GST) we characterize the performance of the single-qubit gates on both electron- and carbon nuclear spins, and analyze the limiting noise processes. items.title: Linear Polarimetry of the Solar Corona during the Total Solar Eclipse of 8 April 2024: Multi-Band Observations and HDR Imaging
items.abstract: High-Dynamic-Range (HDR) multi-band linear polarimetry of the solar corona during total solar eclipses provides a vital ground-based diagnostic tool for mapping plasma morphology and magnetic topology in the inner and middle corona. Extracting reliable polarimetric signals requires rigorous observational calibration, spatial co-alignment, and noise reduction via stacking. We report optical linear polarimetric observations acquired during the 8 April 2024 total solar eclipse from Dallas, Texas, USA, near solar maximum. Using a full-frame color CMOS detector paired with an 80~mm refractor, multi-band Red, Green, and Blue (RGB) images were recorded simultaneously across three polarizer orientations ($-60^\circ$, $0^\circ$, and $+60^\circ$) using a 9-step exposure bracket ($1/800\text{~s}$ to $1/3\text{~s}$). items.title: Privacy-Preserving Robust Monitoring of Dense-Time Temporal Logic
items.abstract: Motivated by the use of third-party testing, this paper presents a privacy-preserving implementation of the robustness monitoring of Signal Temporal Logic (STL). STL is a specification language for systems whose output traces have real-valued timestamps -- most prominently, cyber-physical systems. Its robust semantics, which assign real rather than binary truth values, are an essential ingredient of systems testing and runtime monitoring. In a number of system testing scenarios, the designer and the tester are separate parties. This testing-as-a-service model is common in software, avionics, and semiconductors, and is growing in importance in the red-teaming of machine learning models. In such a model, the designer seeks to preserve the privacy (or secrecy) of its design, while the tester seeks to preserve the privacy of its collateral, including the detailed specification suite. items.title: Superradiant temporal transition radiation of a relativistic electron beam
items.abstract: A charge in uniform motion carries a bound field that does not radiate. Transition radiation releases part of it at a boundary in space. We propose and analyze the case of radiation emission due to a boundary in time: a relativistic electron bunch passes through an aperture in a semiconductor (silicon) wafer, and while its bound field occupies the wafer, a femtosecond laser switches the semiconductor into an electron-hole plasma. The field is a valid solution of the old medium and not of the new one, so it is handed to the plasma as an initial condition for radiation emission at the plasma frequency. Because in temporal transition radiation (t-TR) the wavevector is conserved, and the frequency is not, the emission can appear in a spectral band that the bunch's own field does not populate. items.title: Molecular Doping of MoS$_2$ with N-Heterocyclic Carbenes: A Raman Study of Interfacial Charge Transfer
items.abstract: We demonstrate efficient electron doping of exfoliated MoS$_2$ through the deposition of N-heterocyclic carbene (NHC) molecules onto its surface. Raman spectroscopy reveals a pronounced softening of the optical A$_{1g}$ phonon mode after NHC deposition, consistent with electron transfer from the NHC molecules to the MoS$_2$ layers. The largest phonon-energy shifts are observed in monolayer and bilayer flakes whereas changes in bulk-like MoS$_2$ are negligible, indicating that the doping efficiency depends on the number of layers. This thickness dependence highlights the dominant role of interfacial charge transfer at the NHC/MoS$_2$ interface. Quantitative analysis of the Raman modes of as-exfoliated and NHC-covered MoS$_2$, together with comparison with literature values, allows us to estimate an increase in the two-dimensional electron density of about two-orders of magnitude in MoS$_2...

items.title: Epitaxial Displacement-etched GaAsSb Quantum Dots Emitting at Telecom Wavelengths
items.abstract: Semiconductor quantum dots (QDs) are essential components for integrated photonic and quantum information systems, yet current epitaxial growth techniques face significant limitations in complexity of growth, material selection, and density tunability. Here we report a displacement etch technique that enables controlled formation of GaAsSb QDs with emission at telecommunications wavelengths. Our approach uses arsenic molecular flux (As$_2$) to react with antimonide surfaces through thermodynamically favorable displacement reactions, creating three-dimensional quantum confined nanostructures without requiring strain-driven growth or complex droplet-based processes. items.title: Concatenated continuous-drive protection of exchange-based spin-qubit gates
items.abstract: Exchange-based two-qubit gates in semiconductor spin qubits are sensitive to low-frequency detuning noise and control errors. Here, we extend concatenated continuous driving (CCD), implemented by phase modulation of a global microwave drive, to exchange-based SWAP and $\sqrt{\mathrm{SWAP}}$ operations between double-dressed spin qubits and investigate its effectiveness for protecting two-qubit gates. We find that CCD retains strong protection against quasistatic common-mode detuning errors while substantially improving robustness against Rabi-frequency errors and qubit-to-qubit Rabi-frequency mismatch compared with conventional continuous dressing. By contrast, the gate fidelity is impacted by differential detuning errors. By modeling partially correlated quasistatic detuning noise, we further show that the noise-averaged gate fidelity depends strongly on the spatial correlation of the q...

items.title: Water-Driven Porous Silicon as a Platform for Blue Materials
items.abstract: Living organisms control water to transport matter, transfer energy and drive chemical reactions. In this perspective, we argue that porous silicon can give engineering materials comparable control over water. Its pore architecture, surface chemistry and semiconducting skeleton can be shaped across length scales with the precision of semiconductor processing and, like the water it can host, it relies on one of the most abundant chemical elements on Earth. Liquids in porous silicon, most often water, can flow as a continuum through pores a few nanometers wide, strain the skeleton through capillary and electrosorption stresses, shift structural color, switch transparency, and modulate or generate electrical signals. We describe three directions to combine and extend these effects and overcome their limitations. Pore hierarchy resolves the classical trade-off between interface area and tran...

items.title: Gate-defined quantum dot and charge noise analysis in a Forksheet transistor
items.abstract: We report the cryogenic characterization of a 14-nm nMOS Forksheet transistor down to 10 mK. We demonstrate that the device retains transistor operation with improved characteristics at cryogenic temperatures, while also forming a gate-defined quantum dot that can be tuned to the single-electron regime. In the quantum-dot regime, we perform low-frequency charge-noise measurements across different charge occupations and observe an average charge-noise amplitude of $\langle S_0\rangle = 10\;μ\mathrm{eV}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$ at 1 Hz, with a minimum measured value of $3.3\;μ\mathrm{eV}/\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$. These results highlight the potential of Forksheet technology for the monolithic cointegration of quantum and classical CMOS functionalities in future quantum processors.

items.title: Revealing Detailed Transport Mechanisms in Silicon Tunneling Diodes
items.abstract: Understanding carrier transport in heavily doped semiconductor junctions is essential for developing next-generation tunneling devices for cryogenic electronics and steep-slope technologies. In this work, we investigate the transport mechanisms in a silicon tunneling diode using extensive TCAD (Technology Computer Aided Design) simulations benchmarked against electrical measurements over a wide temperature range of 4 K to 440 K. The measured device characteristics show no negative differential conductance, strong temperature dependence of forward current with a nearly constant semi-logarithmic slope, and weak temperature dependence under high reverse bias. To identify the mechanisms underlying these characteristics, we investigate the contributions of band-to-band tunneling (BTBT), trap-assisted tunneling (TAT), Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) recombination, and avalanche generation. items.title: Engineering nonrelativistic spin splitting in semiconductors by altermagnetic proximity
items.abstract: Altermagnets combine vanishing net magnetization with momentum-dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting, offering functionalities attractive for spintronics and quantum devices. Their practical use, however, is constrained by the limited availability of materials that simultaneously possess the required altermagnetic symmetry, semiconducting electronic structure, and weak spin-orbit coupling. Here we show that these requirements can instead be separated between constituent materials through proximity engineering. We develop an analytical theory for a conventional semiconductor coupled to a gapped $d$-wave altermagnet and demonstrate that virtual tunneling transfers the altermagnetic spin splitting to the semiconductor. Crucially, the induced nonrelativistic and relativistic spin splittings exhibit qualitatively different dependences on band alignment. Virtual processes involving the val...

items.title: Water-Energy-Data nexus reveals sustainability gaps and priorities for AI infrastructure
items.abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) depends on interconnected water, energy, and data systems spanning infrastructure life cycles and diverse geographies, with the potential to intensify water and energy insecurity, exacerbate social inequities and lead to cascading sustainability issues globally. items.abstract: Single-crystal diamond membranes (SCDms) were created using a hydrogen ion-cut process combined with a two-step post-implantation annealing, electrochemical etching, and micro-transfer printing. items.title: From quantum emitters to technological platforms: a perspective on semiconductor quantum dots
items.abstract: Photonic quantum technologies are based on controlled photon states. To generate these, quantum dots have emerged as excellent sources of single and entangled photons. In this Perspective, we briefly review the chronological development of quantum dots as photon sources, from their beginnings as quantum emitters in the early 2000s to the advanced photonic devices being developed today. We highlight the interplay between fundamental research and industrial aspects before discussing the photonic quantum technologies we expect to emerge in the near future.

items.abstract: Area-selective atomic layer deposition (AS-ALD) enables selective material growth for the fabrication of nanoscale semiconductor devices. Predicting inhibitor coverage is essential for understanding and optimizing surface blocking in AS-ALD. Here, we present a computational workflow combining a pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potential with off-lattice grand canonical Monte Carlo simulations and apply it to inhibitor adsorption and precursor blocking on amorphous SiO2. Realistic surface models reveal substantial site-dependent variations in reaction energies and activation barriers, with silanol groups serving as the primary adsorption sites for aminosilane and related inhibitors and metal precursors. items.title: Coherent phonons in photoexcited semiconductors from first principles
items.abstract: Coherent phonons are phase-locked lattice vibrations that provide a sensitive probe of nonequilibrium dynamics in materials. Existing first-principles equation-of-motion (EOM) approaches have successfully described coherent phonons in metals and semimetals, but their extension to semiconductors requires treating the long-lived electron--hole plasma created by above-gap excitation. Here we extend the first-principles EOM framework to photoexcited semiconductors by incorporating the residual plasma force that shifts the lattice equilibrium together with the plasma-induced renormalization of the electronic structure. For monolayer MoTe$_2$, the calculated carrier-density-dependent Te displacement agrees with constrained density-functional perturbation theory only when the renormalized band structure is included. items.title: Programmable Preparation of Topological Entangled States
items.abstract: Programmable preparation of entangled quantum states is a central requirement for scalable quantum information processing, quantum networking and photonic quantum computing. Topological photonic platforms offer an attractive route towards robust quantum-state generation by encoding information in symmetry- protected optical modes, yet the generated entangled states are typically dictated by the lattice geometry and therefore lack programmability. Here we demonstrate programmable preparation of topological entangled states by inverse engineering the nonlinear optical pump profile of an integrated photonic lattice. Our approach enables deterministic control over both the dimensionality and modal structure of the generated entangled state while preserving its topological character. items.title: Trapping of nanofabricated SiO$_2$ high-aspect-ratio discs in an optical lattice
items.abstract: We describe the nanofabrication and loading of lithographically patterned, high aspect ratio $10$ $μ$m diameter silicon dioxide discs with thickness of $400$ nm into an optical standing wave trap in vacuum. We obtain motional spectra of the center of mass motion of the discs using a combination of interferometric and imaging methods. The method is capable of high-efficiency loading and optical trapping using small numbers of objects, of the order of a few particles, with customized geometries and sizes compatible with wafer scale nanofabrication methods. Disc-like particles in optical traps have been identified as promising candidates for detectors of high frequency gravitational waves or as sensitive accelerometers.

items.title: Extended strange metal and superconductivity in partially filled moiré Hubbard bands
items.abstract: Moiré semiconductors provide a physical realization of the Hubbard model. Bandwidth-tuned Mott transitions and complex phase diagrams mimicking those of high-temperature superconductors have been demonstrated near a weak Mott insulating state at half-band-filling. The platform also provides an opportunity to explore the physics of a partially filled Hubbard band at doping densities far away from the Mott insulator, a regime that has remained largely unexplored. Here we report the emergence of an extended strange metal (ESM), in both doping density and twist angle, in a partially filled Hubbard band of twisted bilayer WSe2. The ESM is in the clean limit, persists down to 100mK, and spans over multiple symmetry-breaking ground states; it also appears only at small twist angles, where electronic correlations are strong. items.title: Energetics of Fault-Tolerant Spin-Qubit Quantum Computation
items.abstract: Semiconductor spin qubits offer a promising route to compact and scalable quantum computers, combining long coherence times in isotopically purified silicon with compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing. Beyond computational speedup, their energy efficiency is an important consideration for future large-scale systems. We evaluate the power and energy requirements of a Loss-DiVincenzo spin-qubit quantum computer by analyzing the Quantum Fourier Transform (QFT) and benchmarking it against the classical Fast Fourier Transform (FFT). We develop a detailed energy budget, identifying cryogenic cooling as the dominant baseline contribution before quantum error correction (QEC). items.title: Low magnon damping of a EuSe film down to millikelvin temperatures
items.abstract: The rapid development of quantum magnonics over the past decade has created a demand for magnetic materials that keep their magnon losses low at millikelvin temperatures and add functionality beyond that of the established iron garnets and ferromagnetic metals. items.abstract: A novel silicon allotrope, qtz Si, with quartz topology is proposed and investigated alongside four known allotropes (dia Si-I, lon Si-IV, bsn Si-II, and gsi Si-III) using first-principles density functional theory. qtz Si is found to exhibit the smallest atom-averaged volume (18.06 A3), highest density (2.582 g/cm3), highest bulk modulus (98 GPa), and highest maximum phonon frequency (16 THz) among the five, while showing the lowest shear modulus (37 GPa). items.title: Enabling large language model agents for high-fidelity many-body perturbation theory calculations
items.abstract: Many-body perturbation theory (MBPT) methods, including the GW approximation, the GW plus Bethe-Salpeter equation (GW-BSE) method, and GW perturbation theory (GWPT), among others, provide accurate first-principles descriptions of excited-state properties and multiparticle interactions of materials. However, their use remains limited due to complex multi-software workflows, interdependent physical parameters, and substantial theoretical expertise. Large language model (LLM) agents, which couple a language model to software tools, show potential in automating computational tasks, but MBPT remains an unaddressed challenge. We show that LLM agents tested in our work, including frontier models such as Opus 4.7 and GPT-5.5, do not reliably construct MBPT workflows in one attempt, suggesting that correct setup requires expert knowledge and consistency that current models lack. items.title: Robust Data-Driven Controller Synthesis from Sampled and Uncertain Frequency Response Estimates using Integral Quadratic Constraints
items.abstract: In this paper, we develop a novel MIMO controller synthesis method that relies solely on frequency-domain data of discrete-time systems. The approach is based on an iterative design procedure using \emph{integral quadratic constraints} (IQCs). It generalizes existing data-driven methods that approximate semi-infinite IQC conditions by enforcing them on a finite set of measured frequency points. Such approximations do not provide guarantees on the continuous frequency axis and may fail to capture inter-frequency behavior. We address this limitation by formulating a convex optimization problem that preserves robustness guarantees over the entire frequency range. In particular, the proposed method explicitly accounts for inter-frequency behavior of both plant and controller, leading to certified robust stability and performance. The effectiveness and computational efficiency of the approach...

items.title: The Reciprocal tau-Cell: A Log-Domain Circuit for On-Chip Learning
items.abstract: Training hardware by gradient descent requires a gradient to be computed using a separate backwards pass. If a circuit is reciprocal, meaning every connection is symmetric, the backward pass is the same network run a second time with the error as its input. The reciprocal tau-cell, a weak-inversion log-domain circuit, makes this practical in standard CMOS. Each cell is a current-mode leaky integrator with a built-in ReLU; each connection is two transistors whose signed strength is a ratio of bias currents. The equilibrium of the network is the solution to a convex program, and latching the cells that are off will hardware linearise the circuit, making its second run exactly linear. items.abstract: Ultracool dwarfs are promising targets for detecting and characterising temperate terrestrial exoplanets. Their flux peaks in the near-infrared, beyond the wavelength cut-off of the silicon-based CCDs used by ground-based surveys dedicated to observing them, such as SPECULOOS. We present the on-sky performance of SPIRIT (SPeculoos InfraRed Imager for Transits), an InGaAs CMOS detector on the Callisto telescope at the SPECULOOS Southern Observatory, during its first year of operation, from mid-2022 to 2023. We use 328 visits of 73 targets to optimise our CMOS-specific reduction process, including our approach to glow effects and bad-pixel handling. items.title: CAFE: Conducting-Cell-Aware Adaptive Differential Encoding for Robust DNN Inference in FeFET-Based Compute-in-Memory
items.abstract: Ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET)-based compute-in-memory (CIM) promises energy-efficient deep neural network (DNN) inference, but device variation can severely degrade bit-sliced CIM accuracy. Prior works either rely on hardware modifications or treat such variation as generic noise, overlooking a key FeFET asymmetry: negligible off-state leakage makes errors dominated by conducting on-state cells. This asymmetry is amplified by two's-complement sign extension, which maps small negative values to high-significance bit slices and magnifies their errors during shift-and-add reconstruction. In this paper, we propose CAFE, a conducting-cell-aware adaptive differential encoding framework built upon this FeFET-specific asymmetry. items.abstract: Semiconductor moiré superlattices, owing to strongly bound excitons and pronounced electronic correlation, have emerged as an intriguing solid platform for exploring correlated bosonic phenomena, where the moiré potential landscape plays a central role. Hydrostatic pressure allows continuous, in-situ tuning of this landscape, but remains underexplored because of experimental challenges. We observe distinct pressure evolutions of moiré intralayer excitons, which reveal drastic modulation of the excitonic moiré-potential landscape captured by a continuum model and suggest the capability of engineering the exciton-band topology. items.abstract: Strong coupling between mobile charge carriers or excitons and lattice vibrations gives rise to polarons: quasiparticles formed by charge carriers dressed by a cloud of phonon excitations. Polaron formation determines transport properties of systems ranging from transition-metal oxides and organic semiconductors to light-harvesting complexes. In excitonic systems that admit a hard-core boson description, mapping the excitations to pseudospins provides a natural framework for studying polaron physics, including the nonperturbative regime in which hopping amplitudes, phonon energies, and coupling strengths are comparable. items.title: Single anyons and anyon binding in a quantum Hall dot
items.abstract: Anyons are particles with quantized fractional statistics. In theory, a single anyon can be stabilized as a localized fractional charge within the bulk of a topologically ordered two-dimensional insulator. However, experiments to date have focused on probing anyons in structures in which many anyonic excitations coexist and interact. Here, we demonstrate the trapping of a single anyon in a device consisting of a graphene-based quantum point contact with an embedded tunable quantum Hall dot. Benchmarking our device at v = 1, we demonstrate backscattering between Fermi liquid edge states mediated by the whole-electron Coulomb blockade of the dot. The cleanliness and control available in our device allow depletion of the dot to the last quasihole, and we observe spin blockade for transitions to the opposite-spin Landau level. items.abstract: Ultrafast laser excitation of carriers in semiconductors often results in the creation of fully symmetric coherent optical phonons, typically understood in terms of a thermalized transient carrier population. We test this understanding with systematic measurements and first-principles calculations of the photon-energy dependence of ultrafast-laser-driven coherent phonon generation in tellurium, using excitation wavelengths around the electronic band gap. We observe that, contrary to the expectations of models assuming a thermalized carrier population, the coherent amplitude of the fully symmetric $A_1$ mode changes only weakly when tuning wavelength across the band gap. The measured spectral dependence is instead reproduced by a transition-resolved prethermal force weighted by optical matrix elements and band- and momentum-dependent $A_1$ deformation potentials. The work function is evaluated across a series of low-index nonpolar surfaces. It supports norm-conserving pseudopotentials and the projector augmented-wave (PAW) method with the local-density approximation (LDA) and Perdew-Burke-Ernzerhof (PBE) functionals, Γ-only and explicit k-point sampling, smearing and mixing, forces, stress, relaxation, band structures, densities of states (DOS) and dispersion corrections; execution is serial or MPI-distributed over k-point pools, band groups and plane-wave rows. items.abstract: We develop a theory of ionization-assisted instability that governs the reflection of intense electromagnetic pulses from a semiconductor surface. At high pump repetition rates, the overheating accumulates from pulse to pulse, leading to a gradual rise of the local material temperature and free carrier density - a positive feedback loop that drives thermal runaway. However, this effect competes with diffraction of the pump field on the emerging perturbation of the dielectric permittivity or on the surface relief, which reduces the local electric field amplitude in the overheated regions, thus providing negative feedback. We calculated pair-creation energies of approximately 12.2, 6.5, 7.3, 3.10, and 16.7 eV/pair for AlN, 3C-SiC, 4H-SiC, Si, and SiO2, respectively. items.abstract: Thermodynamic computing lets stochastic physical dynamics carry out a computation and reads out the result as a time average. Recently, thermodynamic computing has been demonstrated on several hardware platforms, including digital CMOS circuits based on stochastic computing. Superconducting single-flux-quantum (SFQ) logic offers very high clock rates and very low switching energy, but it heavily penalizes state, memory, fan-out, and feedback, i.e., exactly the per-neuron accumulators on which such designs rely. We therefore realize thermodynamic computing in SFQ logic through a co-design of a generative model and its circuit in which the datapath holds no state at all. items.abstract: Use of carbon electrodes integrated with CMOS technology has great promise for lab-on-chip, biomedical, environmental, and industrial applications. items.title: TileCas: Cascading Kernel Development Across Programming Abstractions
items.abstract: Programming abstractions have traditionally been designed for humans, but code generation is increasingly performed by models and autonomous agents. We investigate abstractions for machine-driven programming through GPU and AI-accelerator kernel generation. High-level domain-specific languages (DSLs) simplify search by delegating implementation details to compilers, while lower-level representations provide finer-grained control at the cost of a larger and more complex search space. items.title: DFIT: A Framework for Building Instrumentation Tools Across Heterogeneous Dataflow Accelerators
items.abstract: Emerging dataflow accelerators offer exceptional energy efficiency and throughput for machine learning workloads, yet remain largely opaque to developers for performance analysis. Using the 1s, 2p and 2s levels to determine a scalar Rytova-Keldysh Hamiltonian, we test its transfer to the excluded 3p state. The transfer deviations have opposite signs: the observed 3p lies 7.38 meV below the prediction in MoSe2 and 5.58 meV above it in WS2; the opposite signs persist across the complete reported +/-2-sigma peak-error boxes. In a separate high-field-calibrated benchmark, RK removes 66.8% of the orbital error of a pure two-dimensional Coulomb reference, making the remaining state-selective deviations particularly informative. items.title: Evolution and breakdown of chiral anomaly in Weyl semiconductor tellurium
items.abstract: Chiral anomaly in topological materials manifests as negative longitudinal magnetoresistance, yet the tunability and evolution of this effect remain elusive. Here we show that doped tellurium serves as a versatile platform to realize a giant negative longitudinal magnetoresistance that is highly tunable via the Fermi level and magnetic field. By moving the Fermi level towards the Weyl point, we observe a pronounced enhancement of negative magnetoresistance, which arises from chiral anomaly and robustly persists up to ambient temperature. Beyond the quantum limit, the system exhibits positive linear magnetoconductance, serving as a compelling transport signature of the chiral anomaly in the lowest Landau level. Notably, in the extreme quantum limit at cryogenic temperatures, the magnetoresistance undergoes a dramatic reversal from negative to positive. This reversal points to a potential...

items.title: From Prompts to Silicon: Scaling LLM-Assisted Chip Design with the AI Hardware Design League
items.abstract: The semiconductor workforce shortage has renewed interest in making chip design accessible to students without conventional very-large-scale integration (VLSI) training. We present the AI Hardware Design League (AI-HDL), an international, project-based competition in which students use Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate and iteratively refine Verilog while simulation, synthesis, timing analysis, security review, and physical verification provide the engineering feedback needed to validate the result. Across two annual cycles, AI-HDL grew from 172 to 604 participants and from 40 to 108 teams, reaching 30 universities, six community colleges, and 19 countries. In the 2026 cohort, 68.7% of participants reported no prior Verilog experience. Twenty-two teams completed the four design phases and reached final evaluation. items.abstract: Multiterminal Josephson junctions (MTJJs) extend conventional two-terminal Josephson physics to devices defined by multiple superconducting phases, where rich phenomena have been predicted. However, in conventional MTJJs, superconducting transport is often dominated by local coupling between neighboring leads, obscuring physics that goes beyond simple connectivity. Our key observation is a pronounced negative differential longitudinal resistance (NDLR) in the four-probe response near switching currents, while no such feature appears in two-terminal measurements. items.abstract: Most systems trained by equilibrium propagation or coupled learning are in the same class as multi-layer perceptrons: while they may be universal function approximators, they struggle to learn associative tasks which are easy for transformers. The reverse flow is broken by more complex nonlinear systems, such as those performing multiplication which is needed to express dot-product attention. Here we explicitly restore this bidirectional flow by introducing extra circuit elements for this purpose into a double or dyadic circuit. We then use these ideas to construct an attention mechanism exploiting the exponential current law of sub-threshold MOSFET devices. items.title: Effects of chlorine substitution on the magneto-optical properties of CrSBr
items.abstract: We present a systematic study of the effects of chlorine substitution on the magneto-optical properties of the van der Waals layered semiconductor CrSBr. Our study shows that even at substitution level of $x=56\%$ the $\mathrm{CrSBr_{1-x}Cl_{x}}$ material exhibits qualitatively the same clear magneto-optical coupling that was observed in pure CrSBr crystals. items.abstract: Analog transistor sizing, finding design parameters that simultaneously satisfy multiple performance specifications, is a labor-intensive bottleneck in circuit design. items.title: Band Tail States: Speed Bump or End of the Road for Two-Dimensional Semiconductors?
items.abstract: We propose that the path to realizing the full potential of two-dimensional (2D) electronics lies in understanding and mastering their energy band tail states (BTS). Unlike silicon, which benefits from sharp band edges (Urbach energy $E_\rm U$ ~ 10 meV), today's monolayer 2D semiconductors have rough band edges ($E_\rm U$ ~ 100 meV) caused by spatial potential inhomogeneity. Comparing a physics-based electrical model to experiments, we demonstrate that BTS cause reduced effective mobility and "slow" transistor turn-on with excessive gate voltage in monolayer 2D transistors, which sets a fundamental limit for their energy-efficient operation. We also show that BTS effects in 2D transistors could be mitigated with higher gate capacitance, with strain engineering, and by using bilayer instead of monolayer 2D channels, as long as $E_\rm U$ is reduced below ~ 50 meV. items.title: Squeezed light from a semiconductor amplifier
items.abstract: The possibility of generating light in a squeezed quantum state during saturated light amplification in a semiconductor amplifier is theoretically analyzed. Due to four-wave mixing process during amplification, weak components of the spontaneous emission of the medium with symmetric frequency shifts relative to the strong amplified wave acquire the quantum properties of two-mode squeezed light. The squeezing of quadrature components occurs in the range of frequency shifts of several GHz ($\sim$ the inverse relaxation time of the charge carrier density) and can reach 10 dB or more under optimal conditions. The formation of a two-mode squeezing phase facilitates the observation of the squeezing effect, in which a strong wave, playing the role of a local wave, exhibits quadrature noise suppression without additional homodyne detection.

items.title: Hall conductance of dilute electrolytes from odd stochastic density functional theory
items.abstract: Electrolytes under an external magnetic field exhibit a Hall conductivity, much like metals and semiconductors. However, existing theories fail to quantitatively account for their measured Hall conductivities. To make progress toward such a theory, we develop a stochastic density functional framework for electrolytes in a magnetic field. This framework, which we dub odd SDFT, extends the celebrated stochastic density functional theory (SDFT) to incorporate transverse mobilities and chiral time-correlated noise. Using this framework, we calculate the Hall conductivity in the absence of hydrodynamic solvent effects through three approaches: (i) direct response, (ii) Green-Kubo relation, and (iii) a hybrid fluctuation-dissipation relation. We further show that odd SDFT applies more broadly to fluids with broken time-reversal and mirror symmetry, including odd-diffusive fluids and chiral act...

items.title: Theoretical study of nitrogen-vacancy spin coherence enhanced by vacancy aggregation in diamond using cluster-correlation expansion
items.abstract: Annealing a semiconductor makes its vacancies mobile; they aggregate into multi-vacancy complexes that often carry spin. Such centres are a magnetic-noise source for any spin qubit among them, in silicon and silicon carbide as well as in diamond, and they are accordingly blamed for NV- decoherence in irradiated and implanted diamond, with two coherence records credited to removing them. Cluster-correlation-expansion simulations driven by published electron-paramagnetic-resonance parameters invert that attribution. At a fixed paramagnetic spin density a multi-vacancy bath gives a Hahn-echo coherence time 3.1-7.1 times longer than a bath of isolated negative vacancies, over three decades of concentration. A bath dephases the qubit because its spins exchange spin projections with one another, and two can exchange only if their transition frequencies match. A fine-structure splitting shifts...

items.title: Device contacts as spin-state selectors for silicon vacancies in 4H-SiC
items.abstract: Optically addressable defect spins in semiconductors are promising building blocks for scalable quantum technologies. Yet, the consequences of conventional contact schemes used in semiconductor device integration for the quantum spin environment remain largely unexplored. Using the silicon vacancy (V$_\mathrm{Si}$) in silicon carbide (SiC) as a model system, we show that a widely used contact metal, nickel (Ni), intrinsically perturbs the defect spin state and quenches the characteristic emission from the spin-quartet channel of V$_\mathrm{Si}$. Low-energy muon spin rotation further reveals that Ni contacts create a magnetically contaminated region extending at least $\sim$110 nm into the SiC, in stark contrast to non-magnetic contacts such as Ti and Al. To address this challenge, this paper presents a Non-ideality Optimized eNVM Accelerator (NOVA) architecture for on-chip training. Specifically, we first fabricate a two-dimensional (2D) ferroelectric field-effect transistor (FeFET) and develop a conductance modulation behavioral model calibrated with experimental data. Here we investigate octanethiol passivation of sulphur vacancies in monolayer MoS2 field effect transistors, combining x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, photoluminescence, and Raman scattering with electrical transport and optically coupled low-frequency noise spectroscopy. items.title: On-chip nanoplasma for adaptive electromagnetic protection
items.abstract: Over the past decade, semiconductor diodes have served as the primary switching elements in adaptive electromagnetic (EM) protection, yet their performance has been compromised by parasitic effects and thermal accumulation, rendering them inadequate against the rapidly evolving landscape of high-power microwave (HPM) threats. Here we show that on-chip nanoplasma switches (NPMS), composed of gallium nitride electrodes on silicon carbide substrates, exhibit superior radio frequency (RF) and thermal characteristics, positioning them as ideal field-driven switches in RF front-end protectors. By integrating NPMS into metasurfaces, antennas and circuit limiters, we achieve an adaptive response that ensures low-loss transmission for normal signals and high shielding against HPMs, while offering extended operating bandwidth and substantially higher tolerance than conventional solid-state devices...

items.title: Odd-even dichotomy in the waveforms of modified Emden oscillators of arbitrary integer power
items.abstract: Closed-form waveforms of the modified Emden oscillators $\ddot x+(q+2)kx^q\dot x+k^2x^{2q+1}+ω^2x=0$ of arbitrary natural power $q$, and of their damped $c$-deformed versions, are obtained through a generalized commutative factorization that reduces them to Bernoulli equations. We show that commutative factorizations of Liénard equations are gauge-conjugated forms of the nonlocal linearizing transformation of Chandrasekar, Senthilvelan, Kundu and Lakshmanan, the factorization constant being half the difference of the roots of the associated linear oscillator. These oscillators display an odd--even dichotomy: for odd $q$ they are isochronous, with period $2π/ω$ independent of the amplitude, within an explicitly bounded range of the integration constant, while for even $q$ the oscillations decay algebraically, as $t^{-1/q}$. items.abstract: Photonic reservoir computing is a promising physical machine-learning approach for time-series prediction. Quantization of the reservoir response signal is an important consideration in the implementation of photonic reservoir computing, and the number of quantization bits and sampling frequency need to be optimized to achieve high prediction performance and low energy consumption. However, few studies have investigated the effects of the number of quantization bits and sampling frequency on both prediction performance and energy consumption. In this study, we introduce the concept of approximate reservoir computing with a semiconductor laser by quantizing the reservoir node states and output weights. We numerically evaluate the performance of a chaotic time-series prediction task and estimate the energy consumption per sample using a component-level model. By optimizing the number of qu...

items.title: Photon-conserving Raman soliton attractors in focusing and defocusing Kerr media
items.abstract: The sign of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient has long been regarded as irrelevant to the direction of the Raman-induced soliton self-frequency shift. Yet the standard generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) predicts a frequency shift that depends on the sign of the nonlinearity, which leads to an unphysical blue shift in the defocusing case. We resolve this inconsistency by deriving the time-domain form of the photon-conserving GNLSE (pcGNLSE) from its established frequency-domain counterpart. The derivation reveals that photon-number conservation imposes two sign modifications relative to the standard GNLSE: the Raman-shift coefficient acquires the absolute value of the Kerr nonlinear coefficient in place of its signed counterpart, and the self-steepening-Raman dissipation term likewise carries an absolute-value prefactor rather than a signed one. items.title: Graph-Based Kirchhoff Modeling of Non-Ohmic Electron Transport in Self-Assembled Nanonecklace Networks
items.abstract: Gold nanonecklace networks exhibit non-Ohmic current--voltage I-V characteristics with a sharp conduction threshold, making them promising for sensing and transistor-like devices. However, their conduction has been understood largely empirically, because experiments cannot see how conduction evolves inside the network. To address this, we develop a graph-based Kirchhoff modeling framework that resolves these internal processes, tracking the potential and current of every junction. Although every active element conducts linearly, the model reproduces the non-Ohmic response $I \propto (V-V_T)^ζ$. It also captures the experimentally observed effects of junction properties, network density, and voids, which lends confidence to its predicted internal states. These states show that the non-Ohmic response emerges from voltage-driven percolation. Conduction is governed by how junctions are conne...

items.title: Complex frequency-dependent quadrature squeezing in semiconductor lasers
items.abstract: We present a comprehensive study of quadrature squeezing in a quantum well laser based on a fully quantum Langevin approach. We compute the frequency-resolved squeezing map of the laser field and identify optimal squeezing curves, revealing, for the first time to our knowledge, both frequency-dependent squeezing and complex or hidden squeezing in a semiconductor laser. We further analyse the role of the linewidth enhancement factor (alpha-factor) in the emergence of these features. Our results establish semiconductor lasers as a platform for the generation of non-classical light and open new perspectives for their application in quantum communication and sensing.

items.title: Electron state tomography from quasiparticle interference maps
items.abstract: Characterizing electronic band structures requires precise knowledge of wave functions and their quantum geometry. Here, we introduce a tomography method to reconstruct the density matrix of electron states from quasiparticle interference maps around single impurities. We consider two-orbital models on a honeycomb lattice, relevant to graphene heterostructures and direct-gap semiconductors. For on-site impurities, backscattering between time-reversed states directly maps the density matrix populations and coherences into distinct orbital contributions in the interference map. While local probes usually lack orbital resolution, these orbital contributions transform under distinct symmetry group representations and can thus be disentangled to reveal the density matrix and quantum geometric tensor of the scattering states. items.title: Nanoscopic Multiplexing Optical Data Storage via Chip Fabrication
items.abstract: The accelerating growth of global data demands storage technologies combining high capacity, long lifetime and low energy consumption. Optical storage is attractive for archival applications, but conventional optical writing is constrained by diffraction-limited resolution and scalability, while thermal accumulation limits high-speed writing. Here we shift optical data writing from a serial optical process to a fabrication-defined process, in which lithographic masks govern where material modification occurs. Using patterned resist masks and ion implantation, we create fluorescent information voxels with nanoscale control over millimeter-scale areas. items.title: Absorption and Phase-Contrast Microtomography Using Direct X-Ray Detection With Commercial Off-The-Shelf CMOS Sensors
items.abstract: This work presents high-resolution X-ray microtomography based on commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) CMOS image sensors as direct detectors. The system uses a microfocus X-ray source in cone-beam geometry, enabling both absorption-contrast imaging, thanks to the sensor s intrinsic resolution, and phase-contrast imaging, by adjusting the object-to-sensor distance. A dynamic flat-field correction algorithm mitigates radiation-induced sensor degradation during long acquisitions. The setup provides voxel sizes from 3.9 microns to 5.2 microns, with an effective spatial resolution (FWHM) as fine as 9.6 microns in magnified phase-contrast mode (1.33x) and 21 microns in non-magnified absorption-contrast mode. Phase contrast enhances visualization of soft tissue boundaries that are difficult to visualize using absorption-contrast imaging in the same experimental configuration.

items.abstract: Strong light-matter coupling in optical waveguides provides a versatile platform for engineering hybrid polaritonic modes and their dispersion. Using rigorous coupled-wave analysis combined with a coupled-oscillator model, we show that the photonic band structure can be engineered across a range of regimes, from conventional multimode strong coupling to the superstrong coupling regime, where the Rabi splitting becomes comparable to the spacing between adjacent photonic modes. items.title: Energy Consumption in Next Generation Radio Access Networks
items.abstract: Historically, in macro-cell-based networks, the radio access network (RAN) portion accounts for the largest share of energy consumption in mobile networks. With greater densification, the transition to small cells and increased virtualization of the radio processing functions, the relative energy use of the different network segments is changing. At the same time, open radio access networks (O-RAN) have emerged as a promising approach to support this evolution through open interfaces that enable a multi-vendor environment, support for hierarchical intelligent controls, and simplified, cost-effective radio units that facilitate large-scale deployments. This paper examines the impact of these changes on energy consumption in next-generation RAN architectures through transaction-based energy models. items.title: Joint Architecture-Token-Bitwidth Multi-Axis Optimization of Vision Transformers for Semiconductor IC Packaging
items.abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have achieved strong performance in visual recognition, yet their deployment in resource-constrained industrial environments remains limited. The main challenges are their high computational cost, memory requirements, and energy consumption. While individual efficiency techniques such as neural architecture search (NAS), token compression, and low-precision inference have been extensively studied, most prior work targets only a single optimization axis, limiting overall deployment gains while preserving accuracy. In this paper, we present one of the first holistic frameworks that jointly optimizes three complementary axes: architecture, token, and bit-width.
